records.name: Friends of the Free Library of Philadelphia
records.summary: An independent nonprofit that backs the city's Free Library through neighborhood volunteer groups at its branches. It also runs the Book Corner, a shop for new, rare and used books.
records.what_you_do: Join or volunteer with a neighborhood Friends group at a branch, or buy books at the Book Corner. The site does not say how to join, so contact the group to ask.

schedule.text: The Book Corner is open Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm. The site lists no Sunday hours and no regular events.

cost.text: Membership fees are not stated on the site. Books at the Book Corner are sold at reduced prices.

first_step.how: Visit the Book Corner at 311 N. 20th Street during shop hours and ask a bookseller about volunteering, or call (215) 567-0527 or email freelibraryfriends@gmail.com to ask how to join a neighborhood Friends group.
first_step.basis: The Book Corner is open to walk in during posted hours, but the site does not say how to volunteer or join, so the way into the group is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Book Corner is a bookshop with new, rare and used books at low prices, staffed by paid and volunteer booksellers. The site does not describe a volunteer shift or a membership process, so a first visit is mostly browsing and asking questions.
first_visit_tips: Shop hours are Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm.
Look for the shop on Wood Street, a short walk north of the Parkway, near the Central Library.
Call (215) 567-0527 first to ask about volunteering, since the site does not say how.

records.notes: The group's site has no page on joining or volunteering, and its branch list links no neighborhood Friends groups, so the only joining step is asking. Status stays probably_active because the site shows no dated items. Membership fees are not published.

records.name: Friends of the Independence Branch Library
records.summary: Volunteers who raise money, speak up for, and build community around the Independence Branch Library at 18 South 7th Street.
records.what_you_do: Support the branch through fundraising, advocacy and neighborhood ties. Pay yearly dues to become a member, or sign up for the mailing list to hear how to help.

schedule.text: No meetings or events are posted. Membership dues are paid once a year, and renewal notices are sent by letter.

cost.text: Membership dues are at least $10 a year. Extra gifts are welcome and help fund the branch's work.

first_step.how: Mail a membership form with a check for dues to the Friends at 18 South 7th Street, or join online through the Donate button on the group's site. Email friendsindependencebranch@gmail.com first to ask whether the group is meeting now.
first_step.basis: Joining needs annual dues before you learn what the group does day to day, and the site posts no events or volunteer steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical visit, since it posts no meetings or events. Members whose dues are paid up can vote at meetings and elections. The newest news post is from 2023, so ask the group what is happening before you pay.
first_visit_tips: Email the group before you pay to ask what is going on at the branch now.
If you pay by Venmo, use the group's charity profile and put your contact details in the memo.
Expect renewal notices by letter when your dues come due.

records.notes: The newest dated item on the group's own news page is a September 2023 used book sale, so status is set to dormant (evidence older than 24 months). A web search returned a Free Library calendar listing for an August 21, 2026 outdoor event sponsored by the Friends at this branch. That page refused the fetch (403), so nothing from it is used. A person should check it, since it could make the status active. The only price shown is the $10 minimum on the membership page. Verdict is publish, but the owner may want to review it given the dormant status.

records.name: Friends of the Rail Park
records.summary: Volunteers and supporters developing the Rail Park, a three-mile greenway on old rail tracks from Northern Liberties to Fairmount Park. Phase One is already open, and the group runs clean-ups, green-ups and guided tours.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a volunteer clean-up or green-up (each event page has its own registration), book a small-group tour, or come to a park event.

schedule.text: Volunteer clean-ups are held monthly at the park and nearby, and green-ups are posted as separate events. Guided tours are booked through the site. The park is open daily from 7 am to 10 pm.

cost.text: The park and volunteer clean-ups are free. Guided tours have a fee the site does not list. Residents of Pennsylvania and Delaware who hold a qualifying ACCESS or EBT card may book a tour at no cost by contacting the group.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Broad Street Line to Spring Garden station, about a five minute walk. Bus routes 2, 4, 16, 23, 45 and 61 also serve the area. The Noble Street entrance is step-free with an accessible slope, while the Callowhill Street entrance has stairs only. The park has no restrooms.

first_step.how: Register on the event page for a clean-up or green-up, which includes agreeing to a volunteer waiver. To ask about joining the volunteer list, email friends@therailpark.org or call 215-485-2221.
first_step.basis: Clean-ups are open to the public with a sign-up on each event page, and supplies and light refreshments are provided. The site does not say the events suit first timers specifically, so this is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: A clean-up means picking up litter, removing graffiti and helping with general upkeep alongside other volunteers. Supplies are provided and light refreshments are served. Each event page lists its own start and end time, so check it before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Register on the event page first, since signing up includes the waiver.
Enter by the Noble Street entrance, which is step-free. The Callowhill Street side has stairs.
There are no restrooms in the park, so plan ahead.
Pets are welcome in the open park, but non-service pets are not allowed on guided tours.

records.notes: The October 14, 2026 clean-up event page lists 9:30 to 11 pm, which was checked on two reads, so it is a late evening slot. Registration with a waiver is required for each clean-up. The FAQ says clean-ups are monthly and that guided tours have a fee the site does not list. The green-up event page was not read. Volunteer newsletter sign-up is the site's own way to hear about volunteer days.

records.name: Friends of the South Street Police Mini-Station
records.summary: Neighbors and local businesses that support the South Street police mini-station. They raise money for station equipment and upkeep, run community events such as bike rides, and hold toy and clothing drives from time to time.
records.what_you_do: Donate online or by check, sign up for the newsletter, or ask about joining the Communications, Fundraising or Improvements committees through the contact page.

schedule.text: Donation drives and community events come up a few times a year. The site lists no upcoming dates. It mentions a monthly 3rd District police meeting without a date or place.

cost.text: The events the site describes are free to attend, and donations are optional. Donations can be made online through PayPal or by check.

first_step.how: Email policeministation@gmail.com or use the contact page to ask how to help, especially with the Communications, Fundraising or Improvements committees. You can also donate online or by mailed check at any time.
first_step.basis: The site invites volunteers to contact the group about named committees, and its public events are open to residents. It does not describe a volunteer shift or meeting schedule, so the first step is a conversation.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of the group's work is fundraising for the mini-station, such as equipment, bikes and building upkeep. The site asks for volunteers, but it lists no set meetings, so ask the group what volunteers do before you come.
first_visit_tips: Check the newsletter or email the group for the next event, since no upcoming dates are posted.
To mail a donation, use the donation form on the donate page and send a check to PO Box 63894, Philadelphia, PA 19147.

records.notes: The home page mentions toy and winter clothing drops, a 24-hour drop-off at the mini-station, and winter clothing pickup by email to a city police address. The donate page asks for money only and does not mention drop-off, so this record describes money donations and leaves out the drop-off and the city email. Please confirm before publishing. The newest dated item is October 2024 (tier 1), which sits at the 24-month edge of the probably_active rule. Named partners Queen Village Neighbors Association and South Street Police Detail Alliance are in leads_only without URLs.

records.name: Gamelan Gita Santi
records.summary: A Balinese gamelan ensemble in South Philadelphia that teaches traditional Balinese music to community members. Players learn the parts, rehearse as a group, and join the fall concert and community events.
records.what_you_do: Learn to play gamelan parts in a group, rehearse on Thursday evenings, and take part in the fall concert.

schedule.text: Rehearsals are on Thursday evenings, 6:15 to 8:15 pm, during the fall term. Some Saturday sessions at 1:30 pm are led by a guest teaching artist.

cost.text: Not stated on the group's site.

first_step.how: Text 215-254-4475 to register for the fall community sessions.
first_step.basis: Community sessions are open to the public and take sign-ups by text, but the site does not say whether beginners are welcome or what skill is needed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sessions are group rehearsals in which each player learns a part of a piece, and the whole ensemble plays together on the group's gamelan. The site links practice videos of individual parts from each piece's song page, so you can review at home. The site does not list fees or describe a first session, so ask by text before you come.
first_visit_tips: Register by text before you come, since sign-up is by text.
Ask the group whether you can use the practice videos on the song pages before your first session.
The site gives no parking or transit details for PAX, so check the address before you go.

records.notes: The children's practice video page is a resource only and lists no children's sessions, so kids_ok is left out. Named partners on the home page: Modero & Co. (modero.co) was checked and dropped, since it is a dance and cultural company with no public classes, volunteer roles or Philadelphia location listed. Gapura Philadelphia's link returned 404 and was dropped. Thomas Whitman is a person, not a group. The fall concert wording comes from tier 1 and was not repeated on the site in tier 2.

records.name: GameOn!
records.summary: Runs role-playing game camps, after-school programs and classes for kids, and hosts booked game events for parties. Volunteers can sign up through the site.
records.what_you_do: Kids join camps or after-school programs. Volunteers sign up through the volunteer page.

schedule.text: Summer camps run each year, and the site keeps a list of past camps. The site gives no days or times for camps or after-school programs.

cost.text: The site does not show prices. Summer camp registration is handled through Lower Merion Township's registration page.

first_step.how: Use the inquiry form on the site (it asks for your name, email and a comment) to ask about camps and after-school programs, or fill in the volunteer form to join the volunteer list.
first_step.basis: Camps register through another township's page, after-school programs go by email through a link, and the site lists no ages, dates or prices, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a typical session or a first day. The current summer camp is run with Lower Merion Township, so sign-up happens on that township's page. Volunteers who fill in the form are added to a list for events and programs, and the site names two volunteer roles: a manager for RPG business development and an administrative coordinator.
first_visit_tips: Ask for ages, dates and prices before you register, since the site does not list them.
For camp registration, use the Lower Merion Township page that the site links to.
The email address on the connect page is hidden, so call (267) 289-2098 or use the inquiry form.

records.notes: Location is not established. The site shows no street address (the headquarters link leads to a login page). The only camp named is run with Lower Merion Township, a suburb outside the city. The after-school page names one location, a French International School described as in the Philadelphia area, with no address. The owner should decide whether this is out_of_area before it goes live. Status is active because the camps page lists Summer 2026, but no month is given, so no last_sign_of_life is set. No ages, prices or schedules were found for any program. The after-school page says the programs meet Pennsylvania clearance rules for working with children, but it does not say volunteers need clearances, so requirements are left out.

records.name: Garces Foundation (Comunidad Garces)
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs its own programs for immigrants, including English classes, digital skills, free medical and dental care days, and a dental care program. It says it keeps enrolling new students in its English classes.
records.what_you_do: Enroll in an English or digital skills class through its IDIOMA program, volunteer at its health days or at IDIOMA, or use its dental care program. Volunteers with medical or dental training are especially needed for health days.

schedule.text: IDIOMA English and digital skills classes run in 10-week terms, with weekday morning and evening options. Community Health Days are held on Saturdays about every two months, from 9 am to 3 pm.

locations.label: Community Health Days, Philadelphia (Race Street Dental)
Community Health Days, West Grove (Laurel Dental of West Grove)

cost.text: Community Health Days are free. IDIOMA English classes have a $60 course fee, with need-based scholarships and payment plans available.

access.notes: The website is also available in French, Chinese, Arabic, Portuguese and Spanish.

first_step.how: Submit the IDIOMA registration form, pay the $60 course fee (or ask about a scholarship or payment plan), then take the online English placement test on your phone.
first_step.basis: The IDIOMA page lays out each step to enroll, a placement test sets the level, and the site says it keeps enrolling new students. It is not a drop-in class, and there is a fee.
first_step.what_to_expect: Your first step is an English placement test on your phone, which sets your level. Classes last 10 weeks and meet on weekday mornings or evenings. You can attend online or at the BOK Building office in South Philadelphia. The course fee is $60, and scholarships are available. For health days, you call the number for your location to book an appointment, and the care is free.
first_visit_tips: Have your phone ready for the English placement test, since it is taken there.
Ask about a scholarship or payment plan before you pay the course fee.
Call (267) 648-1398 or message that number on WhatsApp with questions about enrolling.

records.notes: Cost is corrected: tier 1 said class fees were not stated, but the IDIOMA page gives a $60 course fee. The IDIOMA page lists office hours (Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm, Friday 9 am to 2 pm), but the contact page lists none, so hours are left out. The contact page gives a separate address for the classes (administrator@garceseducation.org), which is not in the record because contacts holds one email. Dental volunteers need a Pennsylvania radiology certification (volunteer page). The group's focus is Spanish-speaking immigrants with limited English. The site is in several languages, which the notes field records.
